elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.2: "Ono may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, for any reasons..." Ono is our side; this instrument has no Order Form structure, so an Agreement-level right satisfies the element.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Array" replaces the redacted "[ * ] advance written notice" in the original 13.2. The retained rationale-with-notice requirement is a delivery condition, not an extension of the notice period.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case Array shall refund on a pro rata basis any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of such termination" — express pro rata basis stated, not merely a post-termination-period refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: No Array convenience exit appears anywhere in the operative language provided; per the cited Article 13 structure Array's exits are 13.3 material breach and 13.4 bankruptcy (for cause), with 13.5 safety/efficacy terminations running to Ono only. Note the mapping's supporting quote (13.1 Term, "unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13") is not itself dispositive — it merely cross-refers to Article 13; the element is met by the absence of any Array convenience right, and the drafter should cite 13.3–13.4 rather than 13.1.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.2 fixes notice at thirty (30) days, which is below the 60–90 day fallback band (and better for us). The fallback is offered only in the margin comment, which is not operative.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the original nor the rendered 13.2 imposes any early-termination fee, penalty, or contingent payment on Ono's exercise, so no cap is required.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Array holds no convenience termination right at all in the operative text, which is stronger than an end-of-term-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no Array convenience termination right to which a notice period could attach.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (30 days, at any time, express pro rata refund, no Array convenience exit). The fallback level is incomplete only because notice is 30 days rather than 60–90 — that is a Customer-favourable deviation from the fallback band, not a defect.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false, but inspected in substance this is a false negative on the rendered text: revised 13.2 reads "Ono may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time." The check appears to have been run against the original clause, whose right was delayed until the later of two redacted post-First-Commercial-Sale periods and framed as "for any reasons" rather than "for convenience."

Deviation classification is correct: the original 13.2 gave Ono no convenience exit for a multi-year stretch of a term running to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, and fixed no notice period (redacted) — walk-away territory under this rule.

Minimality holds. Deleting the "Commencing on the later of (i)/(ii)..." trigger is necessary to create a right exercisable during the committed term; the notice figure and pro rata refund are required by elements 2 and 3. The drafter retained the heading, "for any reasons," and the rationale-with-notice condition, added no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedure, and correctly omitted "in whole or in part" (surplus here, as there is no Order Form or partial-termination structure).

Intent is preserved: 13.1's "unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13" still resolves, no cross-reference is left dangling, and 13.3–13.5 wind-down mechanics are untouched. One diligence point for the drafter, not a defect on the face of the redline: confirm no retained payment provision (e.g., an upfront/milestone non-refundability sentence in Article 6 or the Article 13 consequences-of-termination section) contradicts the new "Array shall refund on a pro rata basis any prepaid fees" language; if one exists, the refund sentence must be made expressly notwithstanding it or the retained sentence conformed.

Optional tightening (not required for completeness): "prepaid fees" is not a defined term in this agreement, which uses upfront, milestone and royalty payments — consider "any amounts prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination" to avoid an argument that no "fees" were ever prepaid.
